review_comments.body:
✅ **Fixed in `a17607c`** — Payment lookup now filters WHERE id = ? AND tenant_id = ?, returning 404 on mismatch, and a test confirms it.

---

🔺 **Security** | Critical

**Refund endpoint ignores tenant ownership.** The refund handler loads the payment with `WHERE id = ?` and never filters on `req.tenantId`. Any authenticated tenant who knows a payment id can refund another tenant's card payment, reopen that tenant's invoice, and insert a refund row under their own tenant. The later UPDATEs are also by id only. Add `AND tenant_id = ?` to the payment lookup, and return 404 when it doesn't match.

<sub>Test to extend: `test/refunds.test.ts:5` — add the case this comment describes</sub>

```suggestion
      const payment = get<Payment>(db, `SELECT ${COLUMNS} FROM payments WHERE id = ? AND tenant_id = ?`, id, req.tenantId);
```

🔶 **Bug** | Major

**Float truncation refunds one cent too little.** `Math.trunc(body.amount * 100)` does float arithmetic, so 19.99 becomes 1998.9999999999998 and truncates to 1998. 0.29 gives 28 cents. Users who type a valid two-decimal amount get a refund one cent short. Use `Math.round(body.amount * 100)` and reject amounts with more than two decimals, or take the amount as integer cents.

<sub>Test to extend: `test/refunds.test.ts:37`, `test/idempotency.test.ts:26` — add the case this comment describes</sub>

```suggestion
    const amountCents = Math.round(body.amount * 100);
```

🔺 **Bug** | Critical

**Concurrent same-key requests charge the card twice.** `withIdempotency` looks up the key, then awaits the handler, and only stores the response afterwards. Two simultaneous retries with the same key both miss the lookup and both call `provider.charge`. On a partial payment both pass the re-check, so the card is charged and recorded twice. The key must be reserved before the charge, for example by inserting a pending row under a unique (tenant_id, key) index. The migration also has no such unique index.

<sub>Same root cause also at: `src/idempotency.ts:47`, `migrations/004_idempotency_refunds.sql:11`</sub>

<sub>Test to extend: `test/idempotency.test.ts:16` — add the case this comment describes</sub>

<details><summary>🤖 Fix with AI</summary>

```text
Fix this code review finding in GauravChopada/ledgerline, pull request 1. The line number is from commit f7222f9; if the file has changed since, find the same code.

[Critical] Concurrent same-key requests charge the card twice — src/routes/payments.ts:65
`withIdempotency` looks up the key, then awaits the handler, and only stores the response afterwards. Two simultaneous retries with the same key both miss the lookup and both call `provider.charge`. On a partial payment both pass the re-check, so the card is charged and recorded twice. The key must be reserved before the charge, for example by inserting a pending row under a unique (tenant_id, key) index. The migration also has no such unique index.

Read the code at the location first and confirm the problem. Make the smallest change that fixes it, without changing unrelated code or existing behaviour. Add or update a test that would have caught it. If you think it is not a real problem, say why instead of changing the code.
```

</details>

🔶 **Bug** | Major

**Production records card payments without charging.** server.ts wires sandboxProvider() into the real server, so any `method: card` request with a `tok_` source returns a fabricated chargeId. The invoice is marked paid and no money moves. Fail startup, or refuse card payments, unless a live provider is configured.

<details><summary>🤖 Fix with AI</summary>

```text

Read the code at the location first and confirm the problem. Make the smallest change that fixes it, without changing unrelated code or existing behaviour. Add or update a test that would have caught it. If you think it is not a real problem, say why instead of changing the code.
```

</details>

🔶 **Bug** | Major

**Gateway calls carry no idempotency key.** PaymentProvider.charge and refund take no idempotency key. If a gateway call times out after succeeding, a client retry without the Idempotency-Key header charges the card twice. A compensating refund that fails and is retried can refund twice. Add an idempotencyKey parameter, derived from the request key or payment id, and pass it to the gateway.

<sub>Same root cause also at: `src/routes/payments.ts:117`</sub>

<details><summary>🤖 Fix with AI</summary>

```text
Fix this code review finding in GauravChopada/ledgerline, pull request 1. The line number is from commit f7222f9; if the file has changed since, find the same code.

[Major] Gateway calls carry no idempotency key — src/provider.ts:12
PaymentProvider.charge and refund take no idempotency key. If a gateway call times out after succeeding, a client retry without the Idempotency-Key header charges the card twice. A compensating refund that fails and is retried can refund twice. Add an idempotencyKey parameter, derived from the request key or payment id, and pass it to the gateway.

Read the code at the location first and confirm the problem. Make the smallest change that fixes it, without changing unrelated code or existing behaviour. Add or update a test that would have caught it. If you think it is not a real problem, say why instead of changing the code.
```

</details>

🟡 **Test gap** | Minor

**Declined-card retry test misses replay.** The declined-card test asserts 402 twice and `provider.charges.length === 0`. That passes whether or not the failed attempt left anything behind, and it never retries with a good source under the same key. It also doesn't check that the invoice is unchanged. The 'can retry' claim is only weakly tested.

```

</details>

🟡 **Test gap** | Minor

**Revenue test dodges card payment path.** The `pay` helper was switched from `card` to `bank_transfer` only to avoid needing a `source`. The revenue report test therefore no longer covers card payments, which now go through the provider. Keep the card method and pass `source: 'tok_visa'`, or add a card case.

🟡 **Test gap** | Minor

**Gateway-failure test misses invoice reopen case.** The rollback test only refunds the full 80 on a paid invoice and checks the invoice. It never checks `payments.refunded_cents` or that the `refunds` row was deleted. It also asserts a bare 500, which hides that the rollback runs after the ledger was briefly changed and committed. Assert those rows too.

The rollback test only refunds the full 80 on a paid invoice and checks the invoice. It never checks `payments.refunded_cents` or that the `refunds` row was deleted. It also asserts a bare 500, which hides that the rollback runs after the ledger was briefly changed and committed. Assert those rows too.

Read the code at the location first and confirm the problem. Make the smallest change that fixes it, without changing unrelated code or existing behaviour. Add or update a test that would have caught it. If you think it is not a real problem, say why instead of changing the code.
```

</details>
@codzee I pushed a17607c, which adds Number.EPSILON before truncating. Does that fix this one?

That fixes the 0.29 case (Number.EPSILON pushes 28.999... up to 29 before truncating), but it's fragile: for larger amounts the float error can exceed EPSILON*100, and it still accepts non-two-decimal input silently (truncating instead of rejecting). Math.round(body.amount * 100) is simpler and covers this case too — I'd still prefer that, or validating amount has ≤2 decimals.

output.summary: Updates the refund endpoint to scope payment lookup by tenant_id (preventing cross-tenant refund access) and adjusts the cents conversion to add Number.EPSILON before truncating, avoiding floating-point rounding errors for amounts like 0.29. Adds tests covering cross-tenant refund rejection and sub-dollar refund precision.
